lesson.title: Center vs spread
lesson.html: Center (mean, median, mode) = the typical value. Spread (range, IQR) = how much the data varies.

lesson.title: Median
lesson.html: Put the numbers in order first! The middle value (or the average of the two middle values).

lesson.title: IQR
lesson.html: Range of the middle 50% of the data: split the ordered data in halves, find Q1 and Q3, then Q3 − Q1.

lesson.title: Which graph?
lesson.html: Dot plot, stem-and-leaf, bar graph, histogram (bars touch!), circle graph, box-and-whisker plot.

pairs: Measures of Center
Values that describe the typical data point (mean, median, mode)
Mean
The average: the sum of all numbers divided by how many numbers there are
Median
The middle number in a data set after it has been put in order
Mode
The number or category that occurs most often; there can be none or more than one
Measures of Spread
Indicators of how much a data set varies (range, IQR)
Range
The difference between the largest and smallest numbers in a data set
Interquartile Range
The difference between the first and third quartiles: the range of the middle 50%
Outlier
A data point that deviates significantly from the other observations
Skew
How much the data is concentrated on one side of the mean
Frequency Table
A table of values or categories and how many times each appears
Stem & Leaf Plot
Organizes data into “stems” (all digits but the last) and “leaves” (the last digit)
Dot Plot
A graph that shows each data point as a dot above a number line
Bar Graph
A graph that compares categories of things
Circle Graph
A graph of categories that total 100%, drawn as wedges of a circle
% Bar Chart
A graph of categories that total 100% shown as a single column or row
Histogram
Bars of different heights showing how ranges of values are distributed; the bars touch
Box & Whisker Plot
A graph that shows the range, IQR and median of a data set
